purpose: Tactile paper tooth for the light Desk sections
prompt:
A very subtle decorative background texture for a web page section. Warm off-white ground (#FAF9F7) with barely-there tonal variation, a faint diagonal light sweep, and soft low-contrast geometric bands drifting across the frame. Extremely restrained — the texture should be felt rather than seen, never competing with foreground content. Warm-tinted neutrals, no cool grey, matte finish, smooth tonal transitions with no banding. Generous empty space throughout. Purely abstract, minimal and quiet.

An extremely subtle warm paper texture. Uncoated cream stock (#FAF6EE) seen flat and straight on, with a fine irregular fibre tooth and almost imperceptible tonal drift across the sheet. No pattern, no grid, no fold, no shadow, no edges — an infinite continuous surface. Absolutely no people, no words, no logos.

ee1.inspected: File opened and viewed. Not judged from filename, prompt or metadata.
ee1.rationale: A genuinely beautiful warm uncoated paper. Two blocking defects. It does not tile — a directional light sweep crosses the frame, so repeating it at 760px prints a visible grid of sweeps rather than a surface. And it is 2.0 MB, roughly thirty times a defensible budget for a repeating background. Its CSS rule was also dead: it was scoped to [data-register=desk], and nothing in this codebase ever sets that value, so the texture has never rendered on any route. Rule removed in EE1. Needs a seamless tile export at a sane weight before the idea can return.

ee2.inspected: File opened and viewed, then checked against the rendered page in a browser.
ee2.narrativeJob: The House and every interior PageIntro — uncoated stock: the printed programme the desk is set on
ee2.rationale: The tiling defect is designed out rather than fixed: used ONCE, full-bleed, non-repeating, at the scale it was generated for, so the diagonal light sweep reads as light falling across a page instead of a repeating grid. Multiplied at 0.24–0.28 into the ivory ground.
ee2.delivery: next/image, AVIF/WebP, lazy, responsive sizes. Source JPEG is never served.
